title: Single Primary
summary: A single PostgreSQL primary is the default topology for transactional systems. It fits until measured write, availability, or read-isolation requirements justify extra moving parts.
operational_cost: Low relative cost, with normal backup, restore, monitoring, and maintenance responsibilities.
failure_modes: Treating one primary as simple while skipping restore drills or connection limits.

title: Primary With Read Replicas
summary: Read replicas isolate read traffic and improve availability posture for read-heavy or reporting paths. They fit when stale reads are acceptable and lag is observable.
operational_cost: Medium cost because lag, failover behavior, query routing, and replica sizing become product concerns.
failure_modes: Using replicas to hide bad indexes, slow joins, or workloads that require fresh reads.

title: Logical Replication Pair
summary: A logical replication pair moves selected table changes between PostgreSQL databases. It fits migration, fanout, and controlled coexistence when schema scope is explicit.
operational_cost: Medium cost because publications, slots, lag, DDL changes, and conflict expectations need ownership.
failure_modes: Unmonitored slots retain WAL or replicated schemas drift without tests.

title: Logical Replication to Analytics Replica
summary: This topology feeds operational data into an analytics-focused PostgreSQL target. It fits reporting workloads that can tolerate lag and should not scan the primary.
operational_cost: Medium to high cost because freshness contracts, schema transforms, and replay monitoring are now required.
failure_modes: Analytics queries assume primary freshness or silently fall behind during slot lag.

title: postgres_fdw Federation
summary: FDW federation exposes remote PostgreSQL data for bridge reads or limited federation. It fits temporary coexistence, not vague permanent ownership.
operational_cost: Medium cost because network latency, credentials, remote plans, and failure domains enter query execution.
failure_modes: Remote filters fail to push down and hot queries pull large tables over the network.

title: Citus Distributed Cluster
summary: A Citus cluster distributes tables across workers using a distribution key. It fits tenant-local or shard-local workloads after single-node limits are proven.
operational_cost: High cost because backups, rebalancing, shard placement, upgrades, and query locality must be operated deliberately.
failure_modes: Choosing a distribution key that hot queries do not include creates cross-shard work and surprise latency.

title: PgBouncer in Front
summary: PgBouncer in front of PostgreSQL controls client connection pressure and session churn. It fits connection-heavy applications before max_connections becomes the scaling plan.
operational_cost: Medium cost because pool mode, prepared statements, session settings, failover, and observability need review.
failure_modes: Transaction pooling breaks code that assumes session state or LISTEN/NOTIFY behavior.

title: Blue-green Upgrade via Logical Replication
summary: Blue-green upgrade via logical replication builds a new target while the old system continues writing. It fits high-care migrations that need rehearsal and rollback windows.
operational_cost: High cost because dual writes, sequence handling, cutover validation, and rollback criteria must be explicit.
failure_modes: Cutover proceeds without reconciliation queries or a tested reverse path.
